spot.html_text: In the Commentariolus Copernicus listed assumptions that he believed solved the problems of ancient astronomy. Bardi has suggested that these assumptions are non-Euclidean axioms. Copernicus stated that the earth is only the center of gravity and center of the moon’s orbit; that all the spheres encircle the sun, which is close to the center of the universe; that the universe is much larger than previously assumed, and the earth’s distance to the sun is a small fraction of the size of the univers
